messages.content: i want to ask my teacher about a hard page. i understand the first idea but not why the next sentence changes it. help me ask about that part only.
i understand the first idea, but i do not see why the next sentence changes it. could you help me with that part?
can i ask without saying the whole page is impossible?
yes. that message keeps the question about one part, not every part of the page.
say one part.
your question is about one part. it does not say the whole page is impossible.
now the teacher asks me what i think the first idea is. i want to say it in my own words but i am worried it will be wrong.
you can give it as your understanding, not as something you know for sure. i think the first idea is this. then say what you understand.
can you say the first idea for me without seeing the page?
not its real meaning. you would need to give the sentence or tell me about it before i could help with that detail.
can you ask for the sentence?
could you share the sentence you are trying to understand?
what if i only want help making the question, not the answer?
then the first message is enough. you can take it to the teacher without adding an answer you have not worked out.
now only give the message for the teacher.
i understand the first idea, but i do not see why the next sentence changes it. could you help me with that part?
write a story about two friends waiting for a train and thinking again of a question they wanted to ask before.

two friends sat at the station with a little time before their train. one had a book open, while the other watched people walking past. they had talked about a family picture the week before, but one question was still open. the friend with the book remembered it and asked who the person by the tree had been. the other took out her phone and found the picture. she said it was her uncle, not her father as the friend had thought. they looked at the small details together and talked about how similar people in a family can look. when the train came, they put the book and phone away and stood up. the wait had given them time for one question that would have been easy to forget in a busy day.
can you keep the part about the open question simple?
one question was still open from the week before. while waiting, the friend thought of it again and asked who was in the picture.
who was the person by the tree?
the uncle of the friend who had the picture.
did the first friend know that before asking?
no. the first friend had thought it was her father.
what helped them check?
they looked at the picture on the phone, and the person who knew the family gave the answer.
now give the answer in the voice of the friend with the picture.
the person by the tree is my uncle, not my father.
does a similar face mean two people are the same person?
no. different people can look similar. the picture and family context helped with who this one was.
use were and where in simple sentences so i can understand the difference.
we were at home. where is your book? were can be part of a past sentence, while where asks about a place.
now use both in a question about yesterday.
where were you yesterday?
why can both be there?
where asks for the place, and were goes with you in that past question. they do different work in the sentence.
answer it in my voice if i was at the library.
i was at the library yesterday.
why was in the answer instead of were?
with i in that sentence, use was. with you in the question, use were.
now make it about my parents.
where were your parents yesterday?
they were at home. can that be a full answer?
yes. they were at home is a full answer about their place.
now make a question with where and is instead.
where is your book?
if i answer on the table, do you need me to say the whole sentence?
not always. on the table can be enough when the question makes the object clear.
my brother called while i was working. i want to say i can talk later, but i do not know what hour. do not choose one for me.
i am working now, but i would like to talk later. i will let you know when i am free.
can i say i am busy all day if that is not true?
no. you can keep the answer about now without changing it into the whole day.
write a shorter message with now and later.
i cannot talk now, but i would like to talk later. i will let you know when i am free.
what if i want him to send a short message about what it is first?
could you send me a short message about what you want to talk about? i cannot call now, but i can look when i have time.
does that say i have time to read it right away?
not if you keep when i have time. it leaves the reading time open too.
now he says it is only about our visit next week. can i tell him i will call this evening if i have chosen that?
yes. now that you have chosen this evening, you can give that time without making up a specific hour.
only give the message.
i can call this evening to talk about our visit next week.
what if he needs an hour?
then you can choose an hour together. evening gives part of the day, not a specific clock time.
there are three containers. one has two balls, one has one ball, and one is empty. how many balls?
three balls.
how many objects if i count the containers and balls together?
six objects: three containers and three balls.
now i put the one ball into the container that was empty. did the number of balls change?
no. there are still three balls. one container has two, another is empty now, and the last has one.
what if i ask how many containers have balls?
two containers have balls.
can you say the empty container is gone from the room?
no. empty is about what is inside the container in this story, not whether the container is gone.
say empty is about inside.
empty is about what is inside the container, not whether the container is in the room.
now i take away the empty container. how many objects are still there?
five objects are still there: two containers and three balls.
how many balls did i take away?
zero balls, because the container you took was empty.
now only give the number of containers with balls.
two.
write a story about a girl helping her grandfather write a letter. she should ask whose words he wants, rather than add her own ideas without asking.

a girl sat with her grandfather while he wrote to his brother. he asked her for help with a sentence about the garden. she began by saying what she would write, using a long explanation about the flowers. he listened, then said he only wanted to tell his brother that the tree near the door was growing well. she saw that her sentence had made the letter sound like her own story. she asked him what part he most wanted his brother to know. he said the brother had helped plant the tree a long time before. she helped make a short sentence with that idea, then read it back to him. he said it kept the meaning he wanted. she wrote the rest only as he asked, keeping his memory and choices in his own voice.
give the parts about a long time before and his memory.
he said his brother had helped plant the tree a long time before. she kept the memory and his choices in his own voice.
what was wrong with the long sentence?
it added ideas he had not asked for and changed what he wanted to say. that is a meaning problem even if the grammar is right.
keep it simple.
it added ideas he had not asked for and changed what he wanted to say.
can helping with grammar be different from choosing the message?
yes. you can make the sentence more clear while keeping the meaning of the person, rather than choose every idea for them.
use of the person and choose.
you can make the sentence more clear while keeping the meaning of the person, rather than choose every idea for them.
now give a question she could ask before writing the new sentence.
what do you most want your brother to know?
i left a hard page and came back after lunch. i still did not understand everything, but one sentence felt more clear.
that is a real change in understanding, even if the whole page is not clear yet. what is more clear about the sentence now?
i understood who she was talking about.
you understood which person she was talking about. that can help with the next parts.
say it can help with the next parts.
that can help with the next parts, because you know which person the sentence is about.
can i say the break gave every answer?
not if some parts are still hard. you can say one sentence was more clear after the break without making it the answer to everything.
write that in my voice.
i came back after lunch and understood one sentence better. the whole page is not clear yet, but i know who that sentence is about.
does yet make it sound like i might understand later?
it can leave that open. it does not say you will never understand the page.
what if i need to ask someone?
then you can ask about the part that is still hard. knowing one part can help make the next question more specific.
now just a kind reply, no new task.
one part is more clear, and that can be useful learning.
say useful learning.
one part is more clear, and that can be useful learning.
which is right: i will wait until she comes or i will wait until she will come?
for this plan about later, i will wait until she comes is right.
say plan for later.
for this plan about later, i will wait until she comes is right.
why can comes be about later if it is not will come?
after until, comes can be about later because the rest of the sentence gives the plan with will wait.
give another example instead.
i will read until my father calls.
now a sentence with when instead of until.
i will put the book down when my father calls.
what changed?
until gave the end of the reading time. when gives the time for putting the book down.
can i say the father already called from that plan?
no. those sentences give what you will do later, not a fact that the call has happened.
now make it a past story.
i read until my father called. i put the book down when he called.
who did the reading?
the person saying i.
only give the first right sentence again.
i will wait until she comes.
i drew a picture of a garden with a purple tree. help me write one sentence about it without saying real trees must be purple.
i drew a garden with a purple tree in my picture.
can i call it my garden even if the garden is made up?
yes, in a conversation about your drawing, my garden can be your made up garden. if it might sound like a real place, say the garden in my picture.
write that sentence.
the garden in my picture has a purple tree.
what if i want the tree to be small too?
the garden in my picture has a small purple tree.
does adding small change the color?
no. it gives a size detail while keeping purple as the color.
use gives.
it gives a size detail while keeping purple as the color.
now i want to say i chose purple because i liked it. do not make up a larger reason.
i chose purple because i liked it.
can that be enough for a picture i am making for myself?
yes. you can choose a color you like without a reason that works for everyone.
only give the full sentence about the small tree again.
the garden in my picture has a small purple tree.
my friend asked to read a story i started. i am happy she wants to, but i am not ready to show it yet.
you can thank her because she wants to read it and still keep the choice about when to share it.
write a kind message.
thank you for asking. i am not ready to share it yet, but i am happy you want to read it.
what if i do not know whether i will show it later at all?
then do not choose a later time only to make the answer kind. not ready yet can be your answer now, while what happens later is still open.
can i just say i am keeping it for myself now?
yes. i am keeping the story for myself for now. thank you for asking.
does that say what she would think is wrong?
no. it gives your choice to share, not an answer about whether she is right or wrong.
say it is not saying she is wrong.
it is not saying she is wrong. it gives your choice about the story for now.
now only give the message about keeping it for myself.
i am keeping the story for myself for now. thank you for asking.
write a story about a woman using a cup to remember a conversation with her sister. it should be a real cup with no impossible things.

a woman found an old blue cup at the back of a shelf. it had been at the home of her sister during a long visit, and she remembered sitting with it near a window. they had talked about work, family, and a book neither had finished. she did not remember most of the words, but she remembered how easy it had felt to stay there and talk. she washed the cup and used it for tea that evening. the tea was not different because of the cup, and the cup did not bring her sister into the room. it simply gave her a place to begin thinking about the visit again. after a while, she put the cup down and wrote a short message to her sister asking when they could talk again.
can you keep it with home of her sister and remember?
the cup had been at the home of her sister during a long visit. she did not remember every word, but it helped her think about their time together.
did she believe the cup was her sister?
no. the cup helped her remember the visit, but it was an object, not a person.
say it helped with a memory.
the cup helped her remember a visit, but it was still only a cup.
now give the message she could write, short and warm.
i thought about our visit this evening. when would you like to talk again?
does the story say the sister answered?
no. the last part is the woman writing the message. the story does not give an answer from her sister.
only give the last thing that happened.
she wrote a message to her sister asking when they could talk again.
i think i answered my own question while talking. i know what i want to say now.
talking it through can help make your own idea more clear.
can you say something short without making a new plan?
it is good that the words are more clear now.
use more clear.
it is good that the words are more clear now.
now just say goodbye.
goodbye.
with a good afternoon wish, no question.
goodbye. i hope you have a good afternoon.
